answer: The sparrow multiplier is published, charged in copper, and fable lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, as the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 4559 identities would post 4038 proofs and burn roughly 47 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
